newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa Soekor sees first offshore oil in 2 weeks.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa Soekor sees first offshore oil in 2 weeks.

text.p: State-owned oil exploration company Soekor expected to produce its first offshore oil from its Oribi field within two weeks, a spokesman said on Monday.
"We are hoping that we will be able to start producing within the next two weeks," he told Reuters.

"At the moment, they have fitted all the necessary equipment offshore and we are hoping that towards the end of this week we will be able to start testing and commissioning the whole plant," he added.
The oilfield is about 140km south-west of Mossel Bay and is expected to produce 20,000 barrels of oil a day.
The spokesman said that technicians had been able to make up time lost when the Orca oil rig was delayed in Simon's Town harbour undergoing renovations earlier this year.

"Although we left harbour two months late, we have managed to catch up on a lot of that -- probably in the region of three to four weeks. From the time that we start the commissioning and testing, should things run smoothly, it should take about a week to reach full production," he said.

Caltex Oil SA, a Chevron Texaco joint venture, said earlier on Monday it had agreed to take the first full cargo of 600,000 barrels of crude from Oribi for its Cape Town refinery and the Soekor spokesman said that the second cargo would go to a refinery in Durban.
"Durban has requested the second tanker, but I cannot yet confirm which refinery will get it," he said.
The two refineries in Durban are the Sapref refinery jointly run by Shell and British Petroleum and the Engen refinery.
Industry sources said the shipment would probably go to Sapref.

The one-million-barrel shuttle tanker that would ferry the oil from the rig to the refineries had been in Cape Town harbour over the last few weeks and would go to the rig to be connected as soon as commissioning started.
The Soekor spokesman declined to comment on the price of the cargoes.
"There are still sales contracts being negotiated by Caltex and the Central Energy Fund," he said.
The Oribi oilfield is expected to initially produce 20,000 barrels of oil a day, with this amount tapering off over three to six years.

It has probable recoverable reserves of 20 million barrels and will form the nucleus for the subsequent developmentof several other nearby oil discoveries, which could extend production life by a further six years.

Eighty percent of the project's $75 million capital costs have been met by syndicated foreign loans by Soekor and its 20 percent partner, Energy Africa Ltd and the full capital cost of the project is expected to be recovered within a year of operation.

Soekor and Oklahoma-based Phillips Petroleum Co will sign the prospecting lease agreement for blocks 17 and 18 on May 6 in Cape Town. These blocks stretch from the Mozambican border to just south of Durban.
